batchName: Late Republic: Caesar in Gaul (58-50 BCE) - Medium Batch 2
chapterName: Late Republic: Caesar in Gaul (58-50 BCE)

questions.question: What event of 390 BC left Romans with a lasting fear of the Gauls?
options: Gauls had joined Carthage against Rome
The Gauls had sacked Rome itself
Gauls had destroyed a Roman fleet off Ostia
Gauls had captured the port of Massilia
Gauls had killed both consuls in one battle
questions.explanation: Romans never forgot the Gauls' sack of their own city in 390 BC. Yet by Caesar's day the Gallic tribes were prosperous traders who minted coins.
questions.sourceQuote: Yet Romans had never forgotten the Gauls' sack of their own city in 390 BC.

questions.question: How did Ambiorix persuade the commanders of one Roman camp to march out?
options: He claimed all Gaul was rising and Germans were invading
He forged a letter from Caesar ordering a retreat
He offered them gold to abandon the camp
He set fire to their grain stores
He took their envoys as hostages
questions.explanation: Ambiorix spread alarming news and promised safe passage. The Romans believed him and were ambushed in a steep valley.
questions.sourceQuote: He told the commanders of one camp that all of Gaul was rising and the Germans were invading.

questions.question: Caesar claimed a captured census counted 368,000 Helvetii. What do modern estimates suggest for the Helvetii and their allies?
options: About 368,000
questions.explanation: Modern scholars think Caesar hugely inflated the figure. One historian calls him one of history's earliest "spin doctors".
questions.sourceQuote: Modern estimates for the Helvetii and their allies run from 20,000 to 50,000.

questions.question: Which Gallic weakness did Caesar exploit throughout the war?
options: Their ignorance of horses
Their lack of iron weapons
Their dependence on Roman grain
Their small stature in battle
The tribes' rivalries and rare unity
questions.explanation: United, the Gauls could match Rome, but the tribes rarely united. Caesar played on their rivalries again and again.
questions.sourceQuote: The trouble was that the tribes rarely united, and Caesar exploited their rivalries throughout the war.

questions.question: How did Caesar present the Gallic War to his Roman readers?
options: As revenge for the sack of Rome
As a rescue of Roman merchants
As a Senate-ordered punishment
As a defence against barbarians
As a crusade to spread Roman religion
questions.explanation: Caesar framed it as defence, though historians agree it mainly served his career and debts. Gallic and Germanic raids on Roman land were nonetheless real.
questions.sourceQuote: Caesar presented the war as defence against barbarians.

questions.question: What was Vercingetorix's strategy against Caesar's army?
options: Starve the Romans by raiding foragers and burning towns
Ally with Germanic tribes from across the Rhine
Invade the Roman province to draw Caesar south
Ask Pompey for help against Caesar
Meet Caesar in one great pitched battle
questions.explanation: Vercingetorix targeted Rome's weak point, supply. Even after Caesar stormed Avaricum, his alliance held.
questions.sourceQuote: His plan was to starve the Romans by raiding their foragers and burning towns he could not hold.

questions.question: Which honour did the Senate refuse Caesar after his Gallic victories, for political reasons?
options: A seat in the Senate
A triumph
A thanksgiving for Alesia
An extension of his command
A statue on the Capitol
questions.explanation: The Senate decreed 20 days of thanksgiving for Alesia but refused the triumph, the parade that crowned a general's career.
questions.sourceQuote: For political reasons, though, it refused him a triumph (*triumphus*), the parade that crowned a general's career.

questions.question: Why did Caesar crave spectacular headlines in 55 BC?
options: Ambiorix had just destroyed his camps
His Gallic command was about to expire
Pompey and Crassus were consuls and in the spotlight
He had lost a legion to the Nervii
The Senate had just recalled him to Rome
questions.explanation: Renewing their pact in 56 BC gave Caesar five more years in Gaul and his partners the consulship for 55 BC. With his rivals prominent, he needed dramatic feats.
questions.sourceQuote: With these rivals in the spotlight, Caesar needed headlines.

questions.question: According to historians, what did Caesar mainly want from conquering Gaul?
options: Protection for Roman colonists
Plunder and personal glory
Revenge for the sack of Rome
The spread of Roman religion
Grain for the city of Rome
questions.explanation: Historians agree Caesar wanted conquest mainly for plunder and glory; he had ended his consulship deep in debt. The Helvetii migration gave him his excuse for war.
questions.sourceQuote: Historians agree that Caesar wanted conquest mainly for plunder and glory.

questions.question: What helped the Romans defeat the Veneti fleet near Quiberon Bay? (select all that apply)
options: A storm wrecking their oak ships
Grappling hooks shredding their rigging
Germanic allies blocking their harbours
Fire ships sent among their fleet
The wind dying during the battle
questions.explanation: Grappling hooks wrecked the Veneti rigging, then the wind died, leaving their sailing ships helpless against oared Roman galleys. Caesar then executed their elders and sold the rest into slavery.
questions.sourceQuote: There Roman grappling hooks shredded their rigging, and then the wind died, leaving them helpless against oared Roman galleys.
